Another thing I didn't particularly enjoy was the exploration rewards. Most of it is just cosmetic. There's upgrades, yes, but with the rest being cosmetics, I really didn't have the drive to explore as much as I would in another game.

First time playing the game... Spent 8 hours collecting everything I could, exploring everywhere I could. Got to Zeffo, and that was all fine and dandy. Got to a crashed ship in the water, climbed the wreckage (as the game clearly points you to do so, with enemies leading the way). ...And then I jumped into the water. So here's the thing... I had not yet unlocked the Push or Pull ability yet either. Once you jump down from a high ledge and save down low. You are forever trapped to that save location until you save again. I couldn't go anywhere, I couldn't do anything. 8 hours of progress gone.

THERE ARE GAME-BREAKING BUGS.

That said... I tried it again, and saved only after I was sure I had a way out from the save location to the ship. Loved it. I'm still not done, but I am in love with this game. It's so good, and I say that after paying 3 years ago prices for this game, knowing it is going for a fraction of that now. At the price it is now (like $10 Canadian) there is no reason you shouldn't give it a shot. Heed my warnings, and you will love this game too.

Jedi Fallen Order is an amazing star wars game. The story was good, nothing too extreme but not way too simple. However I wouldn't recommend this to someone who has never seen star wars (probably self explanatory but we know how people are). The planets were built and developed very well and some planets )that were visited in the shows for example) are also present here giving you an opportunity to explore them for yourself. The lightsaber customization is pretty in depth, allowing you to customize a good amount of parts on the lightsaber. The combat is also very smooth and pretty easy to learn. Overall it's a great game to play if you're a star wars fan, and because BD-1 is there.

The Jedi series is probably my favorite thing to come out of Star Wars in the last few years aside from Andor. Played this on Steam Deck, ran amazingly after some tweaking, with just a few stutters here and there.

if you like Star Wars, you will most certainly enjoy this game one way or another, the combat and parkour are buttery smooth, the story is well written; the characters are very Star Wars and match the tone well, the planets are detailed, the references are subtle but there and fun to notice, the list goes on. It’s a more than solid game with just a few issues:

- some segments drag on a bit, this game is one of the worst offenders of having those stupid segments where a character is pushing themselves through a crack in the wall

- Im not an amazing gamer, I played through the whole thing on Jedi Master difficulty and had little problem, but some of these bosses were just annoying to fight. (Oggdo)

- Not a universal complaint but as someone who doesn’t do much side content having the healing items be optional was quite annoying, so I finished the whole game with two heals, which wasn’t a big deal but kinda annoying.

Overall a great game, worth the price.

This is the Star Wars game we wanted, Yes a multiplayer shooter was nice too. But what we really wanted was an epic Single Player only story game. And boy, this delivers in freaking spades. It plays wonderfully, with only a few issues (the jumping could be better sometimes). It has an amazing musical score to it, and well, its graphically amazing. It does have some "slight" hiccups on the framerate some times on my pc (5600x / 5600 XT / 32 GB Ram) but for the most part, on my system, it holds a rock solid 75 FPS on High.

I highly recommend this game just for its story alone. It also has a ton of extra collect which are nice, but 100% optional. Also, did i mention there ZERO micro transactions. :) :)

I enjoyed it but I would definitely wait for it to go on sale.

The Good:

-The game can still have that classic Star Wars 'feel' to it. It Makes you feel like Star Wars

-Gameplay, while frustrating at times, is quite enjoyable.

-Hitting enemies with your lightsaber feels great and blocking blaster shots is fun once you get the hang of it.

-Secrets can be fun to look for.

-World looks great and can be fun to explore.

The Bad:

-Movement can definitely feel clunky at time and climbing can sometimes mess up and cost you your life (yes, like Assassin's creed).

-In the beginning the game can feel a bit slow paced and enemies can feel too hard or annoying.

-Often the reward for finding secrets is a chest and chests only contain cosmetic items.

-One of the reasons the game picks up later is that you are able to find more health cartridges, gain more health, and more force as well as abilities. It sometimes feels like the difficulty depends on how much health, force power and cartridges you can hold. I've also found bosses later game to be much easier than some early game bosses due to this.

-I personally feel like some characters would benefit from more spotlight and character development. Especially Greez.

-I wish there was more of a chance to explore some of the planets (make them larger, have extra/side content, etc
It is fantastic, both as a game, and as a Star Wars story. It is a great introduction for those interested in the Star Wars world outside of the films.

I do not recommend buying this game at the current price, but try it through EA Play if you want to give it a shot. Personally I got pretty bored after 10+ hours, but I might change my mind later and give it another shot.

The only things missing in this game are the courage of the studio bosses and their willingness to take any risk. The main character is quite typical. The plot is straightforward, with no complicated decisions or twists. There is no innovation in gameplay — you've seen all these mechanics many times in other games. All of this is already familiar to you.

And despite all that, this is an exceptionally good game. Developers use only proven solutions from other projects but they do it quite ingeniously. Fallen Order has great action, exciting fights, amazing parkour, cool bosses, and, my god, what a stunning soundtrack here.

The first couple of hours tricks you into thinking that this is a game like Uncharted or Tomb Raider. But by the time you realize that it isn't, you've already broken a controller and can no longer get a refund.

UPDATE: Whoever designed that chest on Bogano where you have to do a series of double-jumps and wall runs and rope swings needs to be beaten until they have permanent brain damage. The brain damage needs to be so severe that perform daily tasks like eating and bathing and going to the toilet requires as much skill and concentration as getting that chest.

Great game
But I have to give it a down vote because of controller issues.
I have a PS5 controller. Steam says the game has native support for a PS5 controller, but it obviously doesn't.
When I first opened the game, I had my controller plugged in, and I remember it glitched and defaulted to keyboard settings. There was a message that suggested using a controller was a better way to experience the game.
In the Options menu the game only registers an Xbox controller.
I found a work around for this. I can use my controller with Steam Input on.
Cool
Then the second problem popped up.
Right on the D-Pad is what draws the double-bladed lightsaber. As far as I can tell it doesn't work at all, like it's not mapped. Although it says it is in the steam menu.
I also found a work around for this. I just use the keyboard button any time I want that lightsaber.
But come on, this is ridiculous.
I should not have to find a work around for these essential game functions.
Dev's, if you want people to play with a controller, make sure they can.

A fun and semi challenging souls like Star Wars experience. I really enjoy the story of Cal and the other main characters and cast, There are some really good references and pulls from the Star Wars mythos that I enjoyed, very excellent storyline and writing. The combat is really fun but a lot of this game is map exploration, which I think is really cool and can be really fun but I also tend to get really lost and impatient with running back and forth constantly until I hit an objective, it is a big personal gripe because I do know a lot of people who excel in that type of gameplay more than I. There are some areas where there is noticeable performance issues, but it never crashed or froze up completely, all in all it is a very satisfying and fun game and story to experience, definitely worth picking up whenever it’s on sale.
